sentences.text: Dated this the 10th day of June, 2024  ORDER
The petitioner has submitted Ext.P9 request before the 3 rd respondent for return of the documents mentioned in Ext.P8, submitted before the said authority.

2. A perusal of Ext.P7 mahazar would reveal that an extent of 4.16 Ares of property comprised in Sy.No.176/1-9 of Elamkulam Village in Kanayannoor Taluk was taken over for the purpose of development of the Pulleppady-Thammanam road.

The specific case of the petitioner is that the title deeds of the property has been submitted before the 3rd respondent, which contains other property over and above the 4.16 Ares taken over as per Ext.P7.

The petitioner contends that the title deeds of the property may be handed over to the petitioner after making an endorsement thereon regarding the acquisition of 4.16 Ares of property comprised in Sy. No.176/1-9 of Elamkulam Village in Kanayannoor Taluk.

3. The learned Government Pleader would submit that the petitioner has received 80% of the agreed amount and on receipt of the balance of 20%, it is agreed that it will execute a sale deed in respect of the subject property in favour of the Government.

The learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the petitioner has not executed the sale deed for the reason that he is challenging the amount granted as per the negotiated purchase and the specific contention of the petitioner in the writ petition is that it is entitled for a compensation as per the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (in short 'the Act,
2013).

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The learned Government Pleader would submit that though the petitioner contends that the issue is covered in its favour by the judgment in Shanavas & Anr. v. State of Kerala and Others [2017 (4) KHC 148], a similar issue is pending consideration before the Apex Court and the Court has passed an interim order in the said cases.

entities.text: Shanavas & Anr. v. State of Kerala and Others [2017 (4) KHC 148]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. After hearing both sides I am inclined to pass an interim order directing the 3rd respondent to handover to the petitioner the original of the documents referred in Ext.P8 proceedings, submitted before the said authority, after making an endorsement regarding the acquisition of the property having an extent of 4.16 Ares comprised in Sy. No.176/1-9 of Elamkulam Village in Kanayannoor Taluk, within a period of two weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.

It is also ordered that the petitioner shall execute a sale deed in respect of the property acquired for the purpose of development of the Pulleppady-Thammanam road and receive 20% of the balance amount under protest.

It is made clear that the execution of the sale deed in favour of the Government and receipt of the balance 20% of the amount due to the petitioner will be without prejudice to the contention of the petitioner in the writ petition that it is entitled for a compensation as per the Act, 2013.
